page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 2 vCPUs, 1 physical core, and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 260 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The server is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are notable, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression rates categorized as strong. However, due to the physical constraint of having only 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited. Stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are categorized as poor and weak, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also show constraints, with read-only large block bandwidth at 21.51 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 14.37 GB/sec, both falling into the poor category.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU, the E4-2s_v6 provides a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The presence of Intel AMX instructions supports specialized operations like low-intensity AI inference, though LLM prompt processing for a 7B model is poor at 16.25 tokens/sec. This server is suited for memory-intensive, low-compute tasks such as small-scale caching layers, lightweight database operations, and single-threaded data processing pipelines.
